afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 191822
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1122 AM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- The weather pattern for the rest of the week and well into next
  week will support overall dry and quiet weather conditions 
  across the bulk of the Desert Southwest.

- Temperatures through the period will average a few degrees below
  normal most days with lower desert highs mostly in the upper 
  sixties to the lower seventies. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
As of late this morning visible satellite imagery depicts a large
Pacific closed low straddling the coastline of the Pacific NW. 
This low will gradually weaken, becoming an open wave, as it moves
inland (and practically due east) over the next couple of days. 
The bulk of the forcing associated with this system will remain 
well to our north resulting in the continuation of dry conditions 
across much of the Desert Southwest. There will be a slight bump 
in PWATs tonight and overnight, going from 0.4-0.6" to 0.7-0.8" 
(125-175% of normal). However, this will won't be enough to 
support any rain chances across much of the Desert Southwest, 
especially with the bulk of the forcing remaining to the north. 
Although, there is a slight chance (10-30%) of showers across the 
far western portions of JTNP this evening. The main impact with 
this system will be gusty winds across SE CA from this afternoon 
through the overnight hours. Some occasional gusts over 30 mph 
will be possible across portions of SE CA, mainly Riverside County
and western Imperial County (including the Imperial Valley). Some
gusts near 40 mph will be possible across the typical windy spot 
of the SW corner of Imperial County, resulting in hazardous 
conditions for drivers along I-8, especially high profile 
vehicles. 

This weather system will also help to cool temperatures off back 
below normal. Temperatures today are forecasted to be near normal 
with afternoon highs in the mid 70s across the lower deserts and 
ranging from the mid 60s to low 70s across the higher terrain areas. 
As this trough moves through H5 heights will fall from around 576 dm 
today down to around 570 dm by tomorrow afternoon. This will result 
in cooling temperatures with afternoon highs falling a few 
degrees below normal. Afternoon highs tomorrow are forecasted to 
be in the upper 60s to low 70s across the lower deserts and in the
60s across the higher terrain. Overnight lows tonight will be 
near to slightly above normal with morning lows in the low to mid 
50s across most of the lower deserts and in the 40s across much of
the higher terrain areas. Further cooling will take place Friday 
night and Saturday morning as most lower desert locations will see
morning lows in the 40s with some rural lower desert areas and 
many higher terrain areas expected to bottom out in the 30s. Sub-
freezing lows are likely in portions of JTNP and eastern Gila 
County, and freeze products may be needed for these locations. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH NEXT WEEK/...
Models continue to trend away from any organized disturbance
affecting the Desert Southwest early next week, so it is looking
like the quiet weather will persist through the weekend and 
through at least the first half of next week. Short-wave ridging 
is expected to move through this weekend before a very weak 
shortwave is favored to skim by just to our north on Monday. 
Considerable drying Friday into Saturday is expected to result in 
a dry air mass lasting into early next week keeping clear to 
mostly clear skies in place. Despite the quiet weather conditions 
and passing ridge, temperatures should stay slightly below normal 
over the weekend and into early next week with lower desert highs 
ranging from the upper 60s to the lower 70s and lows mostly in the
40s. 

Uncertainty increases for the latter half of next week with a
slight majority of the GEFS members bringing a Pacific trough 
through the Southwestern U.S. while the rest of the GEFS members 
and the vast majority of the EPS members maintains ridging over 
the region. The most likely outcome for the latter half of next 
week heavily favors continued dry conditions with a slow warming 
trend and temperatures eventually returning to within the normal 
range for late November.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1745Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No major aviation concerns are expected through the TAF period.
Winds will generally follow the typical diurnal trends, with a
brief period of S'rly winds this afternoon, and additional periods
of VRB this evening and tomorrow morning. Wind speeds will be
light aob 8kts. FEW high clouds passing through today before low
lower clouds, near 6kft, through the overnight period, however
will be FEW to SCT at most.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Outside of marginally breezy conditions this afternoon, no major
aviation concerns are expected over the next 24 hours. Forecasted
gusts will hover around 20-25 kt, with some sporadic higher
readings possible, mainly at KIPL. High cirrus coverage will 
decrease through this afternoon, with even a brief period of 
mostly clear skies, before an area of lower bases around 5-7 kft 
moves during the back half of the forecast window. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
A passing weather system will bring breezy to locally windy
conditions across the western districts today into Friday, but 
virtually no chance for precipitation. Relatively dry air will 
remain in place with MinRHs between 30-45% through Friday before 
dropping to 20-30% over the weekend as high pressure briefly
settles into the region. Aside from the increased winds across 
the western districts today into tomorrow, overall light winds 
will prevail. Additional mostly dry disturbances are likely to 
move through or just brush past the region next week bringing 
periods of increased winds but little to no precipitation.
Temperatures will be near normal today but drop to slightly below
normal tomorrow. Temperatures will remain slightly below normal 
through next week as a result of the multiple weather systems 
moving through the region. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to water releases from the dam. 
Water releases remain around 3000 cfs. This will have the 
potential to flood farm fields and low water crossings along the 
river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Berislavich
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Ryan 
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman/Berislavich 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero/Benedict
